concerns.text: FR-006 says "Pearson's r is reported only if the Shapiro-Wilk test indicates normally distributed residuals", but T007 computes and reports "Pearson r (reported alongside ρ)" unconditionally. The task silently relaxes a conditional-reporting requirement (the schema's required pearson_r field forces this, but the task should at least condition or annotate per the spec, or the spec must be amended).

T003 claims data/dataset.csv contains "all columns required by contracts/dataset.schema.yaml" and T004 validates it against that schema, but fingerprint_vector (a required schema field) is only produced in T005. As written, T004 must fail; the task list either needs a pre-encoding schema variant, delayed validation, or reordering — currently the verification step contradicts the contract it cites.

T001 runs "on a small first batch (e.g. 100 entries)" and the Phase-1 checkpoint asserts "≥ 500 (SMILES, pc_raw) pairs", yet no task between T001 and T004 explicitly scales the download to the full set. T004's verification ("logs ≥ 500 valid records") cannot pass on a 100-entry batch. The staging is undocumented in the spec; add an explicit full-download step or make the staging explicit.

T009 tags the threshold sweep {0.5,0.6,0.7} + Bonferroni correction as (FR-008), but FR-008 in the spec is the HTML report requirement; no FR authorizes sensitivity analysis. The task list introduces unrequested scope under a mis-tagged FR — either add a requirement to the spec or drop/narrow the task.

Constitution Principle VII mandates a permutation test with 1,000 iterations logged in results/validation_report.md; T007/T011 hard-require 10,000 shuffles written to data/artifacts/validation_report.json. The task list cannot satisfy both; the constitution must be amended or the artifacts aligned — silently following the spec leaves a constitution violation in every evaluation run.

The acceptance criterion "MAE ≤ 0.05 (PC units)" is never checked: T007 computes MAE but no task asserts or logs pass/fail against the 0.05 threshold. An acceptance criterion from the spec is dropped.

T002 flags pc_raw outside [0, 1] as out-of-bounds while data-model.md flags values outside [0, 10] as erroneous; the spec edge case asks about PC > 1 or < 0. Pick one documented bound and align the task with the data model (or vice versa) so the filter behavior is not contradictory across artifacts.
